entry.text: (Wasted half the night on the same dumb thing again... Now I've got a whole shift ahead to enjoy it.)

break.text: Alright... let's see what made it into the paper this time. Maybe it'll wake me up.

entry.text: Good morning! Seems like my favourite cashier's still alive.
Just saw Father Jean-Noël and the girls outside the church, all tense like they're about to combust, and realised you missed yesterday's Mass. Oh, I have a story for you.
But first, chewing tobacco, please. Yeah, I'm still trapped in it.

response.text: Oh, Gail... Not to pressure you spiritually, but you truly are missing prime entertainment by skipping Mass. Yesterday was... something.
{{erika5mass}}
Locals are pretending they're into it. The tourists we've been attracting lately? Probably regretting stepping inside already.
And right in the middle of all that... in waddles the seal. {{erika5seal}} Pod's handiwork, of course, they'd been whispering and bribing it all morning.
Father tries to ignore it. The seal barks. And this very polished, very not-from-here man just stands up and demands to know what, exactly, is going on.
{{erika5lucie}} Did not calm him.
Father gets sharper. The man gets louder. The seal barks again. I genuinely thought they were about to start a proper fistfight in front of the altar.
But then the man dropped his final dramatic line and stormed out. Everyone stared at the door for a bit, and then Mass just sort of... carried on.
And that was that. Our funny little Sunday.
Mhm... And the seal's still ignoring it, by the way.
Exact same fish, someone else's hand, suddenly it's delicious...
But it's fine. I'm playing the long game.

options.text: Jean-Noël got pissy with me too

response.text: Yeah, he's been pricklier than usual lately. Don't take it too personally, though.

That's kind of his cycle. Funds or donations become cigarettes, wine, or some little whim of his, shady favours go around town... Then something goes sideways and suddenly Father's all bitchy for a week.
He's been doing this trick for years, bless him. That's how the town survives, probably.

options.text: I got one of the nuns' riddles too

response.text: Really? Oh. Good. They've had such long faces lately.
Usually at Mass they're standing there humming along with the organ like proud owners of a singing dog. Now they just sort of... stand there.
But riddles are a good sign, I think.

options.text: Want to tell me something about that bloody note?

response.text: Oh. So you found that.
Umm...
Right, then... Guess that means you...
...Went digging in the rubbish.
...Took the bait and went picking through bin guts for a handful of damp paper... Filthy girl.
Sweet Christ, I'm so glad you did.
Shame it's too late for the ideal scenario, but whatever. It left you with questions, didn't it?
Chewing tobacco. Eel lady hasn't released me from service yet.

options.text: Where did that paper come from?

response.text: Someone left it for me at the newsroom. No name, no return address, just that little treasure map and a bit of blood. Enough to get my attention.
Inside that left side? A whole damned labyrinth. Papers, notebooks, matchboxes, tins, weird little wrapped things - all crammed between pipes or pushed into cavities.
A stash? Some kind of postal system? God knows how long I was in there, elbows deep, trying to figure out what the hell the place even was.
And then - bang - something cracked me on the back of the head. Ears ringing. Floor tilting. Lights out.
Woke up on a pew with Father Jean-Noël rehearsing some sermon draft over me. For a second I thought that was it. Purgatory.

Later... When I finally got another chance to look, the notes, the parcels, the whole delicious mess were already gone. I pulled out half the pipes on that side trying to find even one scrap, but nothing.
Oh. Right. That. When I got knocked out, I'm pretty sure I saw the hem of an altar boy's surplice in the corner of my eye.
And, well... we've got one rather questionable altar boy who 1) has a history of hitting people, 2) is chronically allergic to me, but 3) used to eat sand pies with you.

...Honestly, after the stash evaporated and nothing else twitched for months, I just let the whole thing fade out of my brain. But then with everything bubbling again lately, I thought, hey, maybe the thread isn't dead after all.
Except now, without evidence or the one person I hoped to grill... I've got... nothing, really. No scenario left to act out.
Okay, look... I tried to put everything back how I found it... Ish. I mean, the thing still played at the next Mass, so I convinced myself it was fine.
In my defence, the place was already a mess. I thought if I nudged a few pipes out of place, it wouldn't matter. Like... what's one more crime in a crime scene?
...That's not great, isn't it?
*sigh*
Okay, I'll... sort something out. Make up for this little vandalism somehow.

wrong_items.text: Nope. I need the chewy one.

checkout.text: Thanks. One step closer to today's fish.
Hope you get a nice boring rest of the day. You look like you've earned one. Bye!

entry.text: ...Sorry. Give me a second to settle my thoughts first. I'd rather not add another bad choice to the list.

response.text: *sigh*
...Right. Let's not overthink it.
Thank you for waiting. Yellow Fleuries, please.

wrong_items.text: That's not it, darling. I think... yellow Fleuries might help me.

paying_babetteYes.text: ...Mhm. That's what I needed. You got it before I did.
*sigh* ...Maybe you'll also get why things ended up the way they did.

response.text: Oh. Of course. Sorry, dear. I shouldn't take up your time.
And I suppose you don't really need to know what nail polish can do to old church furniture anyway...

lak.text: Alright... Imagine a quiet afternoon in the Lord's house. Two women of faith on a bench, discussing John 13 and tending to a small matter of foot care.
Then, quite suddenly, they realise a bottle of nail polish may have slipped beneath the bench. And seeped. Onto some rather old and regrettably wooden... ehm, structure.

response.text: Mmm, in theory, yes. But it felt a bit... premature.
Yes, but God tends to appreciate... effort.
Exactly! That's what any sensible person would do, isn't it?
No, dear. That's how small things become bigger ones...

acetone.text: So... You take the acetone and clean it properly. Very properly. To be certain nothing improper remains.
But wood remembers things. And suddenly the Lord's house smells... unmistakable. Mass is approaching. What now?

response.text: ...Mhm. Very honest of you.
No, that won't do. One doesn't answer a mistake with another veil.
Right? It sounds like a good solution.

water.text: Water it is. Feels innocent enough. The scent disappears. No one notices. Peace, briefly, is restored.
A few days later, though, the affected structure looks... swollen. Parts meant to move freely now resist, as if the wood has soaked up more than it ought to. What now?

response.text: Yes... That felt like restoring balance.
Oh, dear. At that point?

drying.text: ...Heat from the radiator. A steady draft through the church. Let it breathe, as they say.
As you might expect by now, it did not help. At the next Mass, a persistent squeaking reached the first pews whenever the music began. So?

response.text: Yes. That's the only truly correct answer. You admit the fault. You don't improvise.

judge.text: Oh no. That would be irresponsible. Interference without understanding only invites further sin.

finale.text: We confessed everything to Father Jean-Noël. Ready for punishment, biblical metaphors, lectures about pride and carelessness.

But no. No fire, no brimstone. He just told us to raise our voices over the worst parts, and asked Noose Boy to swap the hymns for ones with fewer low notes. Convinced him it was a liturgical innovation.
The outcome was... cheerful. Less groaning from the pedals, more from the congregation. Even the shy ones joined in. It was lovely.
...But when it finally gave up completely, Lucie became determined again. Said it was unfair and we ought to do more. I said we'd already done far too much.

She said I was only afraid the Matron would strip us of our little privilege of helping Father Jean-Noël and make us join the rest of the sisters doing tasks we can't stand. I said she wanted heroism where none was needed. Things... escalated.
Perhaps she's not wrong. But I'm afraid her truth will cost us more than we can bear. We'd do the honest thing... and that would be the end of St. Dymphne's for us.

options.text: Nothing you do now will fix it anyway

response.text: Right? I know it's bleak, but it feels honest.

options.text: Leaving it unsaid will only gnaw at you

response.text: You sound exactly like her. I wish either of you were wrong.
But yes... it sits in the ribs, doesn't it. And perhaps it won't stop until we accept whatever comes after.
In the end, I'd rather lose St. Dymphne's than lose Lucie.
You could literally pay for your sins, you know. No confessions. No exile. Very efficient system.
That feels terribly modern and morally ambiguous.
So did nail polish on consecrated wood.
...We don't exactly receive salaries but perhaps we could devise something. Lucie and I can be rather resourceful when we put our heads together.

advice.text: Right. I think I'll go and settle it with Lucie properly. She'll be unbearable for a minute. I will too.
Then we'll share a cigarette and decide things together. As usual.
Thank you, dear. For listening. And for the Fleuries.

checkout.text: Actually... there is one more thing.

checkout_babetteNope.text: ...There is something I wanted to tell you, if you don't mind.

end.text: I didn't mean to involve you, truly... but you've already caught a corner of it, haven't you.
New faces who weren't quite prepared for how we've been doing Mass lately. Then the altar boys brought the seal into the nave. Then that gentleman decided he had something to say...
What I'm trying to say is... it wasn't just Father. We all played our part in that scene, yet it's only his name that was carried to the bishop.
And now it's not just our usual parish gossip anymore, but rather something... administrative.
Anyway... However it ends, and whatever people start saying, I just didn't want you thinking it was simply another one of Father Jean-Noël situations. It wasn't simple. And he wasn't alone in it.
I've taken enough of your time already. God keep you, dear. Preferably in one piece.

entry_decorLateorder.text: Good afternoon. Parcel for the shop. Could you sign here?
Thanks. Oh, look at that, also found a letter for Abigaïl hiding at the bottom. Here.
Hope Abigaïl's about to find for me blue {{jcb}} and three toffees, please.

entry.text: Good afternoon. Got a letter for Abigaïl. Here.
And I hope Abigaïl's got for me blue {{jcb}} and three toffees, please.

click.text: (Hm, he looks healthier than last time. No bandages all over his face. Just the usual dead fish stare.)

response.text: Just give it time. I already nearly drove into the seal earlier.
...Never thought silence on a bike could be that risky.
JC. Blue packet. And three toffee candies. Wrapper with cow spots.

toooth.text: I lost one that ill-fated day in the church... when Father Jean-Noël asked me to help with those boxes. The day I've been trying not to remember.
I was meant to be done for the day.
Just wanted to get home before the rain... But he said since I was already there, maybe I could help him move a few boxes. Like a good Christian.
I said yes... but I didn't want to stay. So I started rushing, not really looking where I was going. Of course it couldn't end well...
My foot caught on something, and the box fell... right onto the poor thing.
I think one of us let out a small cry. Then... only silence, dust, and those white fingers scattered across the floor like dropped dominoes...
I tried to fix it with a toffee I was chewing. Pressed the pieces back together. They stuck, sort of. Sweet and awful.
By white domino fingers you mean...

response.text: You smashed the keyboard with that box? And... thought a toffee would fix that?
Keys? No, no. Whole different corner of the church. The box fell right on the statue of Our Lady.
Oh, her poor little plaster hands...
(God, I'm turning everything into that organ mess now.)
...What? No, I meant... fingers.
Statue... The box fell right on the statue of Our Lady.
Oh, her poor little plaster hands...
Fingers, yes... Oh. But not alive ones, though.
Statue... The box fell right on the statue of Our Lady.
Oh, her poor little plaster hands...

toooth.text: I guess I tore my own tooth out on that same toffee, trying to hide the damage. Wanted to believe since it hurt a little, it would count as repentance. Made me feel a bit less guilty...
But looking at this tooth now... I don't think that's how it works.

wrong_items.text: JC. Blue packet. And three toffee candies. Wrapper with cow spots.

checkout.text: Thanks. Time to get back to work.

checkout_postmanToothGiven.text: ...Hm. Actually, wait a second. Looking closer at the jar, that's not even a front tooth. Mine was front.
So... not mine. Here... take it back.
(And here I thought we'd at least solved one thing.)
Well... That was unnecessary. I'll just... get back to work now.

after_decorLateorder.text: (Alright, mystery parcel. Let's see what's inside.)

options.text: Looks like it came out of a bin
Ugly enough to feel like home

after_decorLateorder.text: There was no sender's name. Just a small card tucked inside: "From your trusted supplier."

break.text: (Right. This should be the inheritance papers for the flat. The whole "it's yours now, do whatever you want with it" part.)
"Following the death of..." yeah, that's her "...the ownership transfer of the property..." that's her stuff...
"...including all associated assets and contents. No other claimants or objections have been recorded... all rights are therefore assigned to the sole lawful heir..."
"...the inheritor is granted full rights to use, manage, or dispose of it at their discretion."
So... that's it. Huh. Her stuff's mine now.

options.text: Sell it and get out of this town

response.text: (Just pay off the debt and leave before these streets start closing in again.)
(No more ghosts knocking on the same doors. Just new air and another chance.)
(This time I'll finally keep my shit together. I'll be ready. I'll be clean. I'll...)

options.text: Stay and try to fix it up

response.text: (Change the wallpaper. Move the furniture. Replace her clutter with my clutter.)
(Stick to small things. The seal. The till. The stupid organ coughing through another Mass.)
(It's probably time to stop pretending there's a version of me that thrives somewhere else. Maybe I'm...)

break.text: (Alright, that's enough thinking for one afternoon.)

entry.text: Over tobacco, rolling papers and matches, please.

response.text: Oh, I mean- just tired. You look tired. Sorry, forget it.
Oh damn. Supposed to avoid smoking then, they say. Heh.

options.text: You look like a lost seal pup

response.text: Heh. Then that makes two lost seals in this town. Maybe someone'll set up a kiddie pool for me too.
Oh. Sorry. Must be glue and shellac. Maybe a bit of pipe dust. Uh... yeah. Sorry. I'll grab the tobacco and vanish, promise.

tired.text: Oh, I mean- just tired. You look tired.
Heh... Guess we've both been playing in the wrong key for a while.

response.text: Over tobacco and matches. ...Oh, and rolling papers. Please.

wrong_items.text: I think you grabbed the wrong one.

after.text: (Let's handle the till and we can finally call it the day.)

entry.text: Hey. Uh, so... I just found something. And... how did that even- Why you-
Sorry, I just... what was that?

response.text: Yeah... probably. I did lose one recently. Never thought it'd still... exist somewhere. Or decide to find its way back.

options.text: I was told to return it to whoever lost it

response.text: Okay... Interesting errand for a tobacco shop, but sure.
Ah... Well.

options.text: What are you gonna do with it?

response.text: ...I don't know. Honestly, I don't really want it.
Funny how someone actually bothered to keep it. And... care? I mean, who ties a little bow on a human leftover? That creeps me out a bit, but in a nice sort of way.
Feels like that bit of me had a better life out there than I could ever give it. So yeah. I don't think I'll keep it.
Mhm. I'll do that, then.

options.text: I think you should keep it

response.text: Um... Sure. Guess I'll... do that, then.
(He clearly won't.)

options.text: Félix might know who it came from

response.text: Oh. Okay. I'll ask him, then. Cool.

options.text: Someone will be glad to take it back

response.text: Really? Oh god. What the-
Incredible. Okay, you know what, I've got an idea.
They asked me to play a bit at Expresso this Friday, I wasn't sure I'd go, but... guess I will.
So if she wants her trophy back, I'll be there.
Oh... and you should come too, of course. If you feel like it. I promise to play something less gloomy than usual.

how_prrckbro.text: *sigh* Okay. Let's say there was a chair and... some rather untrustworthy ceiling hardware involved.
So... I was standing on that chair. Then it went down. Then, apparently, so did I. Met the floor, my face met the chair.
When I woke up, the tooth wasn't there. When I got home, it wasn't there either. Figured that was that.
Now I wonder how it managed to make it all the way... here.

how.text: ...Sorry, I- I don't think I can tell that one.
That's not really a story worth telling anyway.
(Can't blame him. I wouldn't open up to me either.)

end.text: Okay... well then. Thanks, I guess? Um... I'll go, if you don't mind. Have a good evening.

end_prrckbro.text: Funny way to end the day. But... yeah. Thanks.

start.text: (...Why do I even keep smoking the last cigarette of the shift outside?)

salsaRetreat.text: (Yeah, no. I'm cold, tired and not dancing alone in the street because a newspaper told me to.)
(Whatever's sealed in memory can stay there tonight...)
